# MET exploratory evaluation: executable plan (unfrozen, unscored; generated by `make_plan.py` from `eval_plan.json`, sha256 `43943dec5edde2b0…`)

**Evidence scope:** a position-grouped, exploratory comparison of feature sets on public DMS data. It cannot support claims about mutation-induced structural change, transfer to other assays or kinases, or superiority over the authors' published model. No outcome table was read to write this plan.

## Construct, endpoint, eligibility
- Ba/F3 cells expressing the wild-type (exon 14 retained) TPR-MET intracellular domain fusion, IL-3 withdrawal; the exon 14-skipped library (EX_ files) is not used.
- Endpoint γ = ROSACE_effects(inhibitor) - ROSACE_effects(DMSO) for the same variant (the article's gamma = beta_inh - beta_DMSO; log2 fitness scale; wild-type synonymous = 0; each inhibitor dosed at its own IC50, so drugs are modelled separately). Drugs: Crizo, Savo, Mere, A458, Tepo, NVP.
- Eligibility: missense variant with numeric effects in both the inhibitor and the DMSO condition and ROSACE.LOF == FALSE in DMSO (the file's own flag); position inside 1059-1345; no outcome-based filtering otherwise. Expected eligible variants per drug (from the screen): Crizo 1986, Savo 1967, Mere 2036, A458 1950, Tepo 1997, NVP 1906.
- Uncertainty: approximate sd_gamma = sqrt(sd_inh^2 + sd_DMSO^2) from the filtered table, independence assumed although controls are shared; used only for a sensitivity restricted to variants with sd_gamma at or below the median, and as context for the MSE scale. It does not establish a smallest detectable improvement.
- Missing data: exporter masks are final; no imputation. Primary comparison on the common complete-case rows of each drug (L, T and C all available); the same rows and folds for every feature set. The only analysis-side fill: L_min_sidechain_dist_A at glycine sites takes L_min_heavy_dist_A, with an indicator column (documented, training-independent). Missingness (unresolved loops, engineered template residues) is not random: results apply to resolved regions only; coverage by region is reported. Positions with all blocks available: Crizo 270, Savo 232, Mere 249, A458 247, Tepo 273, NVP 232 of 287; in every drug: 172.

## Feature sets and paired comparisons
- **F0:** mutation properties (14 numeric M columns) + drug baseline (per-drug model intercept)
- **F1:** F0 + ligand/site context L (4 columns + glycine indicator)
- **F2:** F1 + 36 Cα distances (C)
- **F3:** F1 + TopoFold angular features T (7 kappa, 6 sin tau, 6 cos tau)
- **F4_optional_external:** F1 + ESM-1b log-likelihood ratio taken from the authors' pre-binning feature file (inputs only; their predictions and model outputs excluded); requires one pinned download of that file (about 7 MB) and verification of the column before use

- **C1** F1 vs F0: what ordinary ligand/site context adds
- **C2** F2 vs F1: Cα distances beyond context
- **C3** F3 vs F1: TopoFold angular features beyond context (primary)
- **C4** F3 vs F2: equal-coordinate head-to-head of the two geometry encodings (primary)
- **C5_optional** F4+T vs F4: angular features beyond a language-model baseline

## Folds, models, metric, decision rule
- Outer: 10 contiguous blocks of positions (29 or 28 each), identical for all feature sets, drugs and models; buffer: training excludes positions within 8 residues of the held-out block on both sides (windows span 4 residues each side, so windows overlap up to separation 8); inner: 5 contiguous blocks over the training positions with the same buffer, for ridge alpha only; grouping: all substitutions and all drugs at a position are held out together. Limits: blocking is in sequence; residues close in space but distant in sequence stay correlated; shared DMSO control and libraries make drugs correlated, so the six drugs are not six independent replicates.
- Models: ridge (per-drug ridge, features standardized on training rows only, alpha in {0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000} chosen by the inner blocks); GBM (per-drug HistGradientBoostingRegressor(max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.05, max_iter=200, min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=1.0, random_state=0), no tuning).
- Primary metric: mean squared error of gamma; within a drug, squared errors averaged per position then over held-out positions with equal position weight; then equal-weight mean over the six drugs; Delta = MSE(a) - MSE(b); negative favours a. Secondary: relative MSE reduction; per-drug Pearson and Spearman correlation (comparable in kind to the correlations the authors report, not on their splits); per-block and per-drug Delta.
- Consistent improvement: Delta < 0 AND the 95% percentile interval of a moving-block bootstrap (blocks of 20 consecutive positions, all drugs resampled together, 2000 resamples) excludes 0 AND Delta < 0 in at least 8 of 10 outer blocks AND in at least 5 of 6 drugs. No improvement: Delta >= 0, or Delta < 0 in at most 5 of 10 outer blocks. Otherwise inconclusive. the same classification for both ridge and GBM; five pre-specified comparisons, no multiplicity correction claimed; intervals are descriptive (coverage not assumed).
- Practical usefulness: separate from the statistical statement: the owner sets a practical threshold on relative MSE reduction before scoring (proposed default 5%); a statistically consistent improvement below it is reported as not practically useful.

## External benchmark
Authors' model: XGBoost on 14 interpretable features including ESM-1b LLR and structural features computed from Umol-predicted inhibitor-bound mutant complexes; trained with 8192 feature combinations; test = all variants of one type I and one type II inhibitor, 20% of positions and two amino acids. Fair and cheap: arm F4 (ESM LLR as an input feature) against F1 under our protocol; descriptive side-by-side of per-inhibitor correlations with the published values, labelled as different splits; no recreation of their model or of Umol structures. Not permitted: any claim of superiority over the authors' model; their strongest competitor uses mutant-complex structure predictions that our wild-type-template features do not have.

## Budget, acceptance conditions, commands
Budget: 20 CPU-minutes, 2 GB RAM; downloads: none required; optional one file of about 7 MB for arm F4.
- plan, evaluation code and tests hash-frozen before the first scoring run
- all input hashes match this plan; exporter freeze verified
- identical row sets and folds across all feature sets (asserted)
- buffer and grouping tests pass on synthetic data (no training row within 8 residues of a held-out block; all substitutions and drugs of a position in the same fold)
- no outcome-dependent feature or row selection; scaling and tuning inside training folds only (tested with a leakage probe on synthetic data)
- results JSON contains every comparison, per-block and per-drug values, coverage and exclusions; report generated from it
- stop and report if any gate fails; a negative or inconclusive outcome completes the task

Commands (the evaluation script is the next task):
```
ulimit -t 1800   # 30 CPU-minute hard cap
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/audit/met_eval_2026-10-28/evaluate.py freeze
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/audit/met_eval_2026-10-28/evaluate.py run
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_met_eval.py -q
```
